dehydrated_text:
They all successively pledged their word and tried to console the distracted women by turning the guilt from the victim of the outrage to the perpetrator and urging that it is the mind that sins, not the body. And where there has been no consent, there is no guilt. It is for you, she said, to see that he gets in deserts.

Okay, so she is raped by the prince and his husband and best friend, Lucius Brutus. They try to console her, but Lucia says, "No, I don't want to be consoled. I want revenge." We are Romans; we fight to the bitter end. If you hit me, I go kill you. If you kill me, I go kill the entire family.

Brutus leads a revolt against the king and forces him out of Rome, making it a republic run by the nobility. People aren't happy with this system because before, if you were good friends with a king, you could do whatever you wanted. Now, you have to follow the laws of Rome. Conspirators include two of Lucius Brutus's sons. They are arrested and condemned to death. Lucius Brutus decides he is going to put his own sons to death.

Youths from noble families stand tied to posts, but all eyes turn to the consul’s children as they are scourged with rods and beheaded. The father's countenance betrays his feelings, but his stern resolution is more apparent as he supervises the public execution.

So, you're a father, right? And these are your two sons. You love them more than anything else in the world. Forced by law to execute your own sons, most fathers would call in sick or go home and sleep until their sons are dead. But Lucas Brutus is like, "No, I'm going to watch my two sons get killed." Not only that, but he organizes their execution.

People are disgusted; they have to look away as the father watches his sons beheaded right before him. His expression shows hatred, disgust, contempt, and guilt. He hates himself more than his sons. The Roman way is to use this energy against an enemy, creating a society so hateful, angry, and vicious that people have all this demonic energy they can use against their enemies.

Now the king decides to attack Rome because the conspiracy has failed. Lucius Brutus rides out to meet the army head on.
